risks.description: The Project channels financing to SMEs/mid-caps via NAFIN through Green Loans (GLs) and Sustainability-Linked Loans (SLLs). For GLs, E&S risk is limited (resources go to a pre-screened positive list), but SLLs operate as corporate loans, making site-specific impacts harder to trace and creating risk around traceability of environmental outcomes and possible greenwashing if sustainability targets are weak or under-monitored.
risks.mitigation: NAFIN prepared an Environmental and Social Management System (ESMS) summary covering main E&S risks by key sector, disclosed at appraisal.

risks.description: Introduction of new financial instruments (notably SLLs) not currently deployed in Mexico, which may lack sufficient demand, drives the technical design risk rating.
risks.mitigation: Substantial TA to NAFIN, PFIs, and beneficiary enterprises (BEs) to support instrument design/deployment; GFPP grant to advance instrument design during preparation; NAFIN required to prepare and adopt a Sustainable Finance Framework (covering SLLs and GLs) acceptable to the Bank prior to effectiveness; draw on global best practices from comparable SLL facilities; Bank hands-on support during initial deployment.

risks.description: The Project requires close coordination and participation of several stakeholders: different units within NAFIN, participating financial institutions (PFIs), beneficiary enterprises, and large anchor companies heading the green value chains (GVCs).
risks.mitigation: Develop and deploy engagement/communication strategies pre-implementation via GFPP plus ongoing TA; establish a dedicated project implementation team within NAFIN with clear roles/responsibilities; formalize PFI participation through legal agreements defining reporting obligations and performance expectations; proactive NAFIN/WB engagement with anchor companies to encourage supplier-firm participation.

risks.description: Risk that SMEs, mid-caps, and participating financial institutions may not take up the new SLL/GL products at the expected pace or scale, given evolving global sustainability policies, limited familiarity with the instruments, and possible overestimation of market demand.
risks.mitigation: NAFIN business-development efforts for sustainable finance; targeted awareness and capacity-building for potential borrowers; TA to help beneficiary enterprises prepare Sustainability Plans and green investment proposals; monitor product uptake with scope to adjust instrument design/eligibility criteria, subject to Bank approval.

notes: Text-driven extraction: Section V (paras 64-67) narrates exactly the 4 SORT categories rated Substantial - Environment and Social, Technical Design, Stakeholders, and 'Other' (SORT row 9, explicitly labeled 'Demand risk' in para 67 and NOT an Overall rating - a genuinely populated 9th category, mapped here to 'other' per project ruling since it does not fit any of the 8 fixed generation categories). The 5 Moderate/Low-rated categories (Political and Governance=Low, Macroeconomic, Sector Strategies, Institutional Capacity, Fiduciary=Moderate) are rated in the SORT table but not discussed in the narrative.
